title: The Crucial Role of TEM Specimen Preparation in STEM EBIC Analysis of Advanced Semiconductor Devices
content: Scanning transmission electron microscopy electron beam-induced current (STEM EBIC) uses a focused electron beam as a localized current source to determine electrical properties at each imaging pixel [1, 2], a crucial technique for semiconductor failure analysis. A related mode, secondary electron emission electric-beam-induced-current (SEEBIC) [1], offers atomic resolution [3] due to the smaller interaction volume associated with secondary electron emission as compared to traditional electron-hole pair separation-based EBIC, especially in thin STEM specimens at high beam energies. STEM EBIC is highly susceptible to artifacts from specimen preparation, particularly Ga focused ion beam (FIB) milling, which can alter the specimen’s electronic properties, surface topography, and SE yield [4]. This work extends previous studies [4,5] on mitigating FIB artifacts via post-FIB Ar ion milling for STEM EBIC by comparing different FIB-prepared TEM specimen configurations.
